items.prompt: Do all plants make flowers?

options.why: Ferns and mosses do not have flowers.

options.text: No, some plants such as ferns and mosses do not.

options.why: Many small plants make flowers too.

hints: Some plants make cones, not flowers.
items.explanation: Not all plants make flowers. Ferns, mosses and conifers do not.

items.prompt: What do the petals of a flower often do?
hints: Bright colours are easy to see.
items.explanation: Bright petals attract insects to the flower.

items.prompt: Which part of a flower protects the bud before it opens?
hints: Think of a bud wrapped in leaves.
items.explanation: The sepals wrap around the bud and protect it.

items.prompt: The ___ is the part of a flower that makes pollen.
hints: It is part of the stamen.
It is at the top of the filament.
items.explanation: The anther makes pollen.

items.prompt: What is the stamen?

options.text: the female part of the flower
options.why: The carpel is the female part.

options.text: the male part of the flower, with an anther and a filament
the green part under the petals

items.explanation: The stamen is the male part of a flower. It has an anther and a filament.

items.prompt: What is the carpel?

options.text: the male part that makes pollen
the female part of the flower, with a stigma, style and ovary

hints: It has an ovary at the bottom.
items.explanation: The carpel is the female part. It has a stigma, a style and an ovary.

items.prompt: Where are the ovules found?
hints: The ovary is at the bottom of the carpel.
items.explanation: The ovules are inside the ovary.

items.prompt: Sort each part into the male or female part of the flower.
hints: The carpel has a sticky top.
items.explanation: The anther and filament are in the stamen. The stigma, style and ovary are in the carpel.

items.prompt: Put the parts of the carpel in order from top to bottom.
hints: The sticky part is on top.
The ovary is at the bottom.
items.explanation: From the top the carpel has the stigma, then the style, then the ovary.

items.prompt: What happens to the ovules after pollination?

options.why: Pollen is made in the anthers.

hints: Seeds form after pollen reaches the ovule.
items.explanation: After pollination the ovules become seeds, and the ovary grows into a fruit.

items.prompt: What happens to the ovary after pollination?

options.text: It dries up and falls off at once.

hints: A mango has a stone in it.
items.explanation: The ovary grows into a fruit that holds the seeds.

items.prompt: Why is the stigma sticky?

options.text: so that pollen sticks to it

hints: Pollen has to land on it.
It is at the top of the carpel.
items.explanation: A sticky stigma holds the pollen grains that land on it.

items.prompt: Which parts belong to the stamen?

options.why: The stigma belongs to the carpel.
The ovary belongs to the carpel.

hints: The stamen is the male part.
The carpel is the other part.
items.explanation: The anther and the filament make up the stamen.

items.prompt: What is the job of a filament?
hints: It is part of the stamen.
items.explanation: The filament is a thin stalk that holds up the anther.

items.prompt: The ___ is the part of a flower that protects the bud before it opens.
items.explanation: Sepals protect the flower while it is a bud.

items.prompt: An insect visits a flower and some pollen sticks to its body. What might happen next?

options.text: It will turn the pollen into seeds.
options.why: Seeds form in the ovary after pollination.

options.text: It may carry the pollen to the stigma of another flower.

hints: Insects travel from flower to flower.
Pollen needs to reach a stigma.
items.explanation: The insect may brush the pollen onto another stigma, which is pollination.

items.prompt: A plant produces seeds but has no flowers or fruit. Which could it be?

options.why: A mango tree has flowers and fruit.

options.text: a conifer such as a pine

hints: Some plants make seeds in cones.
items.explanation: Conifers make seeds in cones and do not have flowers.

items.prompt: If you removed all the anthers from a flower, what could not happen?

options.text: The flower could not grow petals.
The flower could not make its own pollen.
The flower could not make a fruit at all.
options.why: It might still get pollen from another flower.

items.explanation: Without anthers the flower would not make any pollen.

items.prompt: Why do flowers that are pollinated by insects usually have bright petals?

options.text: Bright petals help insects find the flower.

items.explanation: Bright petals act like a sign that tells insects where the nectar is.

items.prompt: A scientist wants to stop a flower from making seeds. Which is the best way?

options.why: Pollen can still reach the stigma.

options.text: Cover the flower so that no pollen reaches the stigma.

items.explanation: Seeds only form after pollen reaches the stigma, so covering the flower stops pollination.

items.prompt: True or false: The petals of a flower can attract insects.
items.explanation: Bright colours and scent bring insects, which help with pollination.

items.prompt: True or false: The stigma is the part of the flower that makes pollen.
items.explanation: The anther makes pollen. The stigma is the sticky top of the female part that catches pollen.

items.prompt: True or false: Seeds develop from the ovules in the ovary of a flower after fertilisation.
items.explanation: The ovary holds the ovules. After pollination and fertilisation they become seeds.

items.prompt: True or false: All plants make flowers to produce new plants.
items.explanation: Some plants, such as mosses and ferns, do not make flowers. They reproduce using spores.
